newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-NEW UNITS, ADVANCES LIFT INVESTEC.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-NEW UNITS, ADVANCES LIFT INVESTEC.

text.p: First-time contributions from new operations and strong domestic asset growth is seen propelling annual earnings growth at Investec Group Ltd, an acquisitive South African banking and financial services firm.

Analysts said on Friday Investec, known in the marketplace for its aggressive marketing strategies, would for the third year in a row show a diluted earnings jump of over 30 percent, cutting into the market share of the country's bigger banks.
The bank is due to report results for the year ended March 31 on Wednesday.
"They are definitely making inroads into the retail market although it is a very selective market," said Justin Kretzschmar, an analyst at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
"They have made their mark taking business away at the top end of the big four (banks) in terms of business clients."

Investec, which has a largely professional and high net worth client base, is also seen reaping foreign exchange rewards as earnings from new and existing offshore operations are translated back into South African rands.

Investec last June bought a 52 percent stake in Israel General Bank, that country's then eighth largest bank, for $48 million. In October it bought British porfolio management stockbroker, Carr Sheppards, which has more than 2.5 billion stg in funds under management.

"There are new contributions for the first time from some of the acquisitions from last year and they have also made some exchange rate transaction gains," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
Investec last year also took over South African stockbroker Fergusson Bros.
Robust growth in advances last year, pegged at around 44 percent, was seen boosting bottom line diluted share earnings by some six percent.
"They only got half of the benefit last year and the rest will filter through now," another analyst said.
Associates' earnings were expected to add two percent.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast diluted earnings per share for the year rising to between 550.0 and 558.3 cents with consensus at 552.8 from 419.8 a year ago -- a rise of almost 32 percent.
They expected the dividend to increase to between 250.0 and 269.0 cents a share, with estimates averaging out at 261.7 from 200.0 before.

Looking ahead, analysts raised concerns about stiffer competition for Investec's key earner, its private banking unit which offers lending and investment products to select professional clients, as other banks set up similar operations.
"Others are going for that slice of the assets. It is a very competitive," Kretzschmar said.
